title: Mean absolute coordinate Laplacian
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite type, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega)\to\mathbb{R}$, and let $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. The product Laplacian $L^1$ quantity at coordinate $i$ is the product mean of the absolute value of the coordinate Laplacian of $f$ at $i$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$f$ is a real-valued function on $n$-tuples from $\Omega$
caveat: The snippet refers to the coordinate Laplacian and product mean through definitions not included in the payload, so the Laplacian's precise convention is unavailable.
